refute_b.reason: 'The National Security Space Launch (NSSL)' is owned verbatim by two PEs — NSSL00 (doc 416 procurement) and 1206853SF (doc 417, EMD, which owns 'Launch Service Agreement (LSA)') — but the record discriminates in its own words: a firm-fixed-price modification buying 'launch vehicle production services' for an operational NRO Launch Mission Three is a procured launch, not EMD or an LSA; the residual is that this record is truncated at 700 characters before the funding sentence, so the appropriation is never stated outright.

proposals.announcement_evidence: systems engineering, management, and sustainment (SEMS) III
proposals.rationale: Rejected by §3 design: the contract is generic services — 'systems engineering, systems/program management, and sustainment services' for an organization's enterprise information systems — with no named program element. The only near-name in the index is 'Air Force Weather Service (AFWS)' under 1203940SF, and the announcement's 'Air Force Weather Agency' is the customer ORGANIZATION, not that program; the index row moreover sits under the title 'Space Situation Awareness Operations'. A $300M IDIQ for enterprise SE and sustainment is precisely the generic-services pattern the rubric rejects.

proposals.announcement_evidence: F-15 Combined (V)3 and Radar Modernization Program (RMP) radar upgrades
proposals.rationale: Rejected as a name collision across programs (§3 / Lens B pattern). 'Radar Modernization Program (RMP)' is carried in the F index only as the B-52 Radar Modernization Program, under B05200 (doc 407, 'B-52') and 0101113F ('B-52 Squadrons'). This award is the F-15 RMP — 17 (V)3 and 29 RMP radars for F-15 aircraft from Boeing St. Louis — an entirely different radar program that happens to share the generic phrase. The F index carries no F-15 RMP name; 'F-15 Radar Enhancements (RE)' under 0207134F is a different effort and is not named in the announcement, and matching on the bare designator F-15 would be platform matching, which §3 also rejects.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Taiwan MQ-9B SkyGuardian procurement
proposals.rationale: Rejected on two §3/Lens-B grounds. First, the announcement is about a different variant: MQ-9B SkyGuardian is the export derivative, and the index carries no SkyGuardian or MQ-9B name at all — only 'MQ-9 UAV' and 'MQ-9 System Lifecycle Agile Modernization (SLAM)' under the RDT&E PE 0205219F, plus 'MQ-9 Mods' under PRDTB2. Second, the award is 100% foreign military sales to Taiwan, obligating FMS funds, so it funds no U.S. budget line at all; attributing it to a U.S. PE would assert work the PE did not pay for.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Taiwan MQ-9B SkyGuardian procurement
proposals.rationale: Same rejection as record 21 on the earlier award against the same contract number: MQ-9B SkyGuardian is a variant the F index does not carry under any name, and the buy is Foreign Military Sales to Taiwan funded with FMS money, so no U.S. program element pays for it. Matching on the bare MQ-9 designator to 'MQ-9 UAV' would be a designator-variant error of exactly the kind Lens B is meant to catch.

proposals.announcement_evidence: contractor operated and maintained base supply services for the T-6A/B/D Texan II aircraft
proposals.rationale: Rejected by §3 design: contractor operated and maintained base supply (COMBS) is generic logistics — 'serviceable aircraft material and support equipment' across a dozen Air Force, Navy and Army bases — not the work of a named program element. The only candidate is the bare designator T-6 under JPAT00 (doc 407, aircraft procurement), which is the platform the supply contract supports rather than the program the line funds, and a base-supply services contract is not an aircraft-procurement action.

proposals.announcement_evidence: to support the Sentinel-Ground Based Strategic Deterrent weapon system
proposals.rationale: Rejected by §3 design: the contract itself is a $200M IDIQ ceiling for 'research and development services in support of the nuclear enterprise' — generic R&D support, with Sentinel named only as what the first task order supports. The index's only Sentinel program row is LGM-35A Sentinel under MGBSD0, a doc-410 MISSILE PROCUREMENT line, while the task order obligates fiscal 2022 RDT&E funds; support services charged to RDT&E cannot be attributed to a procurement line. The named weapon system is the thing the support contract supports, not the program the line buys.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Belgium MQ-9B SkyGuardian procurement
proposals.rationale: Same rejection as records 21 and 38: MQ-9B SkyGuardian is an export variant the F index carries under no name, and the procurement is Foreign Military Sales to Belgium funded entirely with FMS money ($94,341,260 obligated), so no U.S. program element funds this work. Linking it to 'MQ-9 UAV' would assert that a U.S. RDT&E line paid for a foreign air force's aircraft.

proposals.announcement_evidence: F-15 Radar Modernization Program (RMP) radar upgrades
proposals.rationale: Rejected as the same cross-program name collision found at record 5, here on a later modification to the same contract. The F index owns 'Radar Modernization Program (RMP)' only as the B-52 RMP (B05200 doc 407, and 0101113F doc 412); this award buys Group A and B kits, conformal fuel tanks and RMP isopods for F-15s at Boeing St. Louis. A different program owns the name, so the evidence is a string resemblance rather than an attribution.

proposals.announcement_evidence: F-15 Saudi Arabia Depot prime vendor support services
proposals.rationale: Rejected by §3 design on two counts: the scope is generic logistics — 'procurement services, warehousing, and bench stocking of unclassified consumables and spares' — and the only candidate name is the bare platform designator F-15 (the index carries 'F-15E' under F01500 and 'F-15EX' under F015EX), which is the aircraft the support contract serves, not a program the line funds. The work is also entirely foreign military sales for the Royal Saudi Air Force, so no U.S. budget line pays for it.

proposals.announcement_evidence: task order for Sentinel support
proposals.rationale: Rejected by §3 design: the task order's own description is generic engineering support — 'continuing the strategic partnership between government and JHU/APL', providing 'engineering, systems engineering for complex systems, research, and development of specialized functions' — which is the engineering-support pattern the rubric rejects regardless of the program named in the title. The index's only Sentinel program row, LGM-35A Sentinel, sits on the doc-410 missile-procurement line MGBSD0, while this task order obligates fiscal 2023 RDT&E funds, so the appropriation does not match either.

proposals.announcement_evidence: support for repair, maintenance and modification of F-15, F-16, UH1N, C-130 and other required aircraft
proposals.rationale: Rejected by §3 design: the Eglin backshop maintenance services contract is generic base maintenance across four unrelated aircraft types plus support equipment and crash recovery — no named program. The only index candidates are bare platform designators (F-15E under F01500, T-6, etc.), and §3 rejects naming a platform the contract supports as if it were the program a line funds. A maintenance services contract is not an aircraft-procurement action either.

proposals.announcement_evidence: F-15SA Original Equipment Manufacturer Training Program
proposals.rationale: Rejected by §3 design and by variant mismatch: the award is 100% foreign military sales to Saudi Arabia for an OEM training program performed at three Saudi air bases, so no U.S. program element funds it, and F-15SA is a Saudi-specific variant the F index carries under no name — the closest rows are 'F-15E' (F01500) and 'F-15EX' (F015EX), different aircraft. Matching on the shared F-15 designator would be the platform/variant error the rubric rejects.

proposals.announcement_evidence: contractor operated and maintained base supply non-personal services for the Joint Primary Training System T-6A/B Texan II aircraft
proposals.rationale: Rejected by §3 design, same pattern as record 46: contractor operated and maintained base supply is generic logistics services, funded here with fiscal 2016 Air Force and Navy operations and maintenance money. The only index candidate is the bare designator T-6 under the doc-407 aircraft-procurement line JPAT00 — the platform the supply contract serves, and the wrong appropriation for an O&M services option.

proposals.announcement_evidence: MQ-9 Reaper production
proposals.rationale: The MQ-9 designator is present and the award is unambiguously the MQ-9 program's own work — production of MQ-9 Reaper aircraft in the fiscal 2017 configuration, obligating fiscal 2016 and 2017 AIRCRAFT PROCUREMENT funds. But the F index carries no MQ-9 production line: the candidates are 'MQ-9 UAV' under the RDT&E PE 0205219F and 'MQ-9 Mods' under PRDTB2, a modification line. Attaching an aircraft-procurement new-build to an RDT&E PE is the appropriation failure mode Lens A exists to catch, and the aircraft are not modifications, so neither member can carry the claim. Not linked.

proposals.announcement_evidence: MQ-9 Reaper unmanned aerial systems support and services
proposals.rationale: The MQ-9 name is present, but the scope is O&M sustainment — program management, logistics support, configuration management, depot repair, field service representatives — obligating fiscal 2019 operations and maintenance funds. The index's MQ-9 members are an RDT&E PE (0205219F 'MQ-9 UAV') and a procurement modification line (PRDTB2 'MQ-9 Mods'); O&M sustainment attached to either is exactly the failure the held-out study found. Not linked.

proposals.announcement_evidence: MQ-9 Reaper production under Basic Ordering Agreement
proposals.rationale: Same shortfall as record 2: 24 MQ-9 Block 5 aircraft with spares and support equipment, bought with fiscal 2013 and 2014 aircraft procurement funds. The F index has no MQ-9 production line — only the RDT&E PE 0205219F and the PRDTB2 modification line — so no index member can be said to fund a new-build buy. Not linked.

proposals.program_name: F119 Aircraft Engine Component Improvement Program
proposals.announcement_evidence: F119 engine sustainment
proposals.rationale: 'F119' matches the index name's leading designator, but the index row is the F119 Aircraft Engine COMPONENT IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM under the RDT&E PE 0207268F, and the award is field sustainment of fielded F119 engines across eleven bases, obligating fiscal 2015 procurement and operations funds. Engine sustainment is not component improvement, and O&M/procurement sustainment attached to an RDT&E CIP line is the documented failure mode. Not linked.

proposals.program_name: F119 Aircraft Engine Component Improvement Program
proposals.announcement_evidence: F119 Engine Sustainment
proposals.rationale: Same shortfall as record 11 on a later modification to the same contract: fiscal 2015 operations and maintenance and Air National Guard funds pay for sustainment of fielded F119 engines, while the only F119 row in the index is the RDT&E Component Improvement Program line 0207268F. O&M sustainment on an RDT&E line does not meet the evidence standard. Not linked.

proposals.announcement_evidence: MQ-9 Reaper production
proposals.rationale: Production of MQ-9 Reaper aircraft in the fiscal 2018 configuration with fiscal 2017 and 2018 aircraft procurement funds. As at records 2 and 9, the F index offers only an RDT&E PE ('MQ-9 UAV', 0205219F) and a modification line ('MQ-9 Mods', PRDTB2); neither funds new-build airframes, so the designator match does not establish that this award paid for either line's own work. Not linked.

proposals.announcement_evidence: MQ-9 Contract Aircrew Training and Courseware Development training program
proposals.rationale: The MQ-9 designator appears, but the award is an aircrew training and courseware services contract at Creech, Holloman, March and Hancock Field, funded with fiscal 2019 operations and maintenance money. The index carries no MQ-9 training line — its only 'Aircrew Training System (ATS)' rows belong to the KC-46A — and O&M training services cannot be attributed to the RDT&E PE 0205219F or the PRDTB2 modification line. Not linked.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Next Generation Overhead Persistent Infrared Polar Space Vehicles 1 and 2
proposals.rationale: The award is plainly Next Generation OPIR work — Polar Space Vehicles 1 and 2 — and 1206442SF is the Next Generation OPIR PE. But the F index carries NO name row for the program itself under that PE: its four names are 'Blossom Point Tracking Facility (BPTF)', 'Boulder Ground Innovation Facility (BGIF)', 'Factory Reach Back Center (FRBC)' and the SMI row quoted here, none of which appears in the announcement and none of which is the Polar space-vehicle effort. Proposing any of them would name a sub-effort the contract is not for, so the proposal is recorded as weak rather than linked; the gap is in the lexicon, not in the announcement.

proposals.program_name: LGM-30G Flight Test Telemetry and Termination System (FT3)
proposals.announcement_evidence: flight test telemetry termination production requirements contract
proposals.rationale: The description matches the index name closely — 'flight test telemetry termination' against 'LGM-30G Flight Test Telemetry and Termination System (FT3)' — and the Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center at Hill AFB is the right contracting activity for Minuteman III. But the announcement calls it a PRODUCTION requirements contract while 0101213F 'Minuteman Squadrons' is an RDT&E PE, and 'No funds are being obligated at the time of award', so the appropriation cannot be confirmed from the record. Under the rule to default against linking when uncertain, this stays weak.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Battlefield Airborne Communications Node payload operation and support
proposals.rationale: BACN is named verbatim, but two things block a link. The award is payload OPERATION and support for a further year, obligating fiscal 2020 operations and maintenance funds ($20,000,000) — O&M services, while 834050 is a doc-411 procurement line. And the name is owned by five different index members (834050, 0207238F 'E-11A', E011A0 and E011A1 'E-11 BACN/HAG', and OTHACF 'Other Aircraft'), so the announcement's words cannot say which line the money belongs to. Not linked.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Evolved Expendable Launch Vehicle (EELV) Phase I contract
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the Evolved Expendable Launch Vehicle program, which was later renamed National Security Space Launch — the only launch-program name the index carries. But 'EELV' appears nowhere in the F index, so the link would rest on an out-of-record rename rather than on the announcement's own words, and this 2017 modification buys an Atlas V 551 configuration plus an ELC option, which straddles launch capability and launch services. A rename alias that the record itself does not evidence does not meet the standard. Not linked.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Global Hawk contractor logistic services and sustainment
proposals.rationale: Global Hawk is the RQ-4, which the index carries under the RDT&E PE 0305220F 'RQ-4 UAV', so an alias is available. But the award is contractor logistics support — planning, operations support and maintenance support — obligating fiscal 2016 operations and maintenance funds ($68,855,210), and O&M sustainment attached to an RDT&E line is the failure mode Lens A is written against. Global Hawk is also the platform the CLS contract supports rather than a program the PE develops. Not linked.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Global Hawk contractor logistic services and Sustainment III
proposals.rationale: Same shortfall as record 44 on an earlier option of the same contract: replenishment spares, repairs, contractor field teams, inventory control and organizational maintenance manpower are O&M sustainment, while the only Global Hawk/RQ-4 index members are the RDT&E PE 0305220F and a sensor-operator trainer under 0305206F. The alias holds; the attribution does not. Not linked.

proposals.announcement_evidence: space based infrared system contractor logistics support
proposals.rationale: SBIRS is named, but the award is contractor logistics support at the operating locations (Peterson, Buckley, Greeley, Boulder) obligating fiscal 2020 operations and maintenance funds — O&M sustainment, while SPCMOD is a doc-416 space PROCUREMENT line. SPCMOD 'Space Mods' is also a rollup carrying twenty-six unrelated names (BMEWS, PARCS, GPS ground antennas, solar observing networks and more), which §3 and Lens A treat as a catch-all rather than a program a single award can be attributed to. Not linked.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Battlefield Airborne Communications Node, payload operations and sustainment
proposals.rationale: Same shortfall as record 39 on the Option Year One exercise of the same contract: payload operations and sustainment paid with fiscal 2019 overseas contingency operations and operations and maintenance funds ($149,616,524) cannot be attributed to the doc-411 procurement line 834050, and the BACN name is owned by five separate index members across three J-books, so the announcement cannot say which one. Not linked.
